summary: Quick sync on week 2 pilot results: Redwood shows 15-22% lower median latency on 1k token prompts vs CloudAIServe baseline under similar instance sizing; however tail-latency (p99) gaps remain in burst scenarios. SE recommended tweaks: increase continuous batching window for steady traffic, enable prefix KV caching for repeat conversations, and try 4-bit quantization profile for cost savings with small quality checks. Next steps: share artifacts, run head-to-head load, and present dedicated slot sizing/pricing for pilot expansion.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-29   Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jasper Liu (Redwood), Markus Chen (GlacierPoint CTO), Aisha Rahman (Head of MLOps), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Renee Park (Product), Speaker 6

[00:00] Liam Ortega: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know we have a full plate today. quick agenda — bench readout vs baseline, triage the p99 spikes, and decide on next steps for the dedicated slot request.
[00:18] Markus Chen: great, thanks Liam. we ran the synthetic and prod-ish prompt sets overnight, saw your numbers in the dashboard, wanted to walk through anomalies.
[00:32] Priya Nair: yeah hi — i'll start with the key metrics. for the 1k token prompt set, median latency on Redwood runtime is ~320ms versus CloudAIServe at ~380ms, so about 15-16% improvement in medians. throughput at steady state was about 12k tokens/sec per GPU node versus 10.6k on baseline.
[01:05] Aisha Rahman: that matches what we glanced at. but the p99 is a different story — on burst traffic we see Redwood at ~1.7s vs baseline ~1.4s. curious what's driving that tail.
[01:20] Priya Nair: yeah that's the thing — most of the p99s we traced line up with cold kv-cache misses and heavy cross-rack communication during autoscaling events. when the queue spiked the batching window pushed larger which increased token aggregation but caused queuing for a small subset.
[01:41] Diego Alvarez: would that be avoidable by changing batching window? in prod we care about p95/p99 more than median.
[01:50] Priya Nair: definitely tunable. two levers — reduce max batching window to keep tail lower (cost goes up slightly) or keep larger windows but add graceful degradation to a smaller, lower-cost model variant for tails. we also recommend enabling prefix KV caching for conversation reuse which reduced p99 in our lab by ~20% for repeat-turn flows.
[02:15] Markus Chen: can you explain prefix KV cache — we probably mis-labeled in our notes earlier?
[02:21] Priya Nair: sure — it's the ability to reuse previous key-value attention caches for repeated prefixes so you don't re-run earlier tokens. it helps when you have multi-turn with repeated context. implementation-wise it's a flag on the runtime that increases memory usage but cuts repeated decoding time.
[02:40] Jasper Liu: and to add — we saw in the trace that 40% of p99 events were on sessions with high conversation reuse, so the cache would have big wins.
[02:52] Renee Park: is there any risk to model quality with KV caching or quant? we need to show product and clinical stakeholders no regressions.
[03:02] Priya Nair: KV cache is quality-neutral. quantization is where we need small checks — our 4-bit profile (q4) preserved pass-rate on your eval set at 98.7% vs fp16 baseline but you need to validate on your edge prompts.
[03:20] Aisha Rahman: interesting — any examples of failure modes with q4?
[03:25] Priya Nair: edge numeric hallucinations slightly more often in niche prompts (like uncommon clinical codes). we can gate q4 on lower-sensitivity routes or run a quality-sampling pipeline.
[03:36] Markus Chen: cost impact?
[03:39] Jasper Liu: roughly 30-40% lower per-token compute cost vs fp16 when using q4 in our bench. combined with batching and caching you can see 45-55% unit cost reduction depending on traffic.
[03:52] Diego Alvarez: ok that helps. about dedicated slots — we requested a 4-GPU dedicated pool for the pilot, the question is whether the observed performance justifies reserved capacity.
[04:02] Liam Ortega: right — our suggestion: start with a 2xA100 equivalent dedicated pool for pilot (approx sizing we'll share) to get stable tail-latency. dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor autoscaling events and keeps p99 tighter; costs more but predictable.
[04:18] Aisha Rahman: could you quantify the p99 delta we should expect moving dedicated?
[04:22] Priya Nair: from our lab sims, p99 improved ~25-35% moving to dedicated for bursty workloads at similar throughput. your current p99 of 1.7s could drop to ~1.1–1.3s in typical bursts.
[04:39] Markus Chen: that would be compelling. any security or compliance blockers for dedicated?
[04:44] Liam Ortega: no technical blocker — dedicated provides isolation, we can enable customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integration for keys. we'll provide SOC2 and audit docs.
[04:56] Renee Park: on the head-to-head results, the baseline vendor used a slightly different batching policy; are you normalizing for that?
[05:04] Priya Nair: good call — we re-ran the baseline with a normalized batching window and same model size where possible. differences remain due to kernel choices and routing — CloudAIServe uses a smaller KV cache by default and different compilation kernels causing the median delta. we included both raw and normalized spreadsheets.
[05:24] Markus Chen: i noticed a weird spike at ~12:34 in your trace, can we walk that?
[05:29] Priya Nair: sure — that's an autoscaler event where an instance was preempted during a burst, we fell back to a slower instance for ~6s. we've flagged that as unusual — not typical in our hosted infra, likely test harness artifact.
[05:45] Diego Alvarez: so to be clear we should re-run the head-to-head with deterministic instance pool?
[05:50] Priya Nair: yes please, we recommend pinning instance types and disabling preemption for the head-to-head.
[05:58] Liam Ortega: quick question from pricing perspective — Markus, what is your target SLA for p99 and what's the acceptable unit-cost range?
[06:08] Markus Chen: p99 ideally under 1.2s for 95% of traffic; unit cost we'd like to be no more than 20% over our current vendor at parity quality.
[06:19] Jasper Liu: that's reasonable — with q4 on low-risk routes and caching we can likely hit both, but need the head-to-head to be sure.
[06:29] Aisha Rahman: are there any telemetry hooks we should enable to better correlate user experience with bench data?
[06:36] Priya Nair: yes — enable token-level tracing and per-route sampling (we'll provide a schema). also push KV cache hit metrics and batch size histograms into your observability so you can map p99 to queuing vs compute.
[06:51] Markus Chen: can you also include a simple script to replay a subset of production traffic? helps validate end-to-end.
[06:58] Liam Ortega: we can provide a small replay harness — sanitized — that can run against both endpoints.
[07:05] Renee Park: timeline question — if we get good head-to-head results, how fast could you provision a dedicated pilot?
[07:12] Liam Ortega: typically 2–3 business days after contract/slot confirmation. we'll need the sizing confirmed and an internal ticket to provisioning.
[07:20] Diego Alvarez: one more technical — during heavy batching are KV caches pinned in memory? we saw OOM events in an earlier run.
[07:29] Priya Nair: good catch — caches are memory resident; you can either increase node memory or evict older prefixes. we recommend LRU eviction with a cap to avoid OOM — we'll send recommended memory sizing.
[07:41] Markus Chen: ok good. i'd like that recommended sizing in the same doc as the cost estimate.
[07:47] Liam Ortega: noted.
[07:50] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[08:00] Priya Nair: i'll also note our suggestion to gate q4 to non-sensitive endpoints and sample for quality. plus a rollback plan in case we see drift.
[08:12] Aisha Rahman: what's the expected change in throughput when moving q4? any latency regresses?
[08:18] Jasper Liu: throughput appears to improve slightly because kernel throughput is better for q4 in our tests — median latency was stable, tail sometimes improved because of lower compute. but, again, must validate on your prompts.
[08:32] Markus Chen: sound plan. let's recap and clarify owners.
[08:37] Liam Ortega: recap: Redwood shares bench spreadsheet + traces (Liam) and tail traces/KV metrics (Priya). GlacierPoint runs deterministic head-to-head and shares results (Diego). Redwood SEs propose dedicated slot sizing & cost (Jasper/Priya). schedule exec review for 2026-06-03 (Liam).
[09:00] Aisha Rahman: agreed. any outstanding legal or procurement notes?
[09:06] Liam Ortega: procurement asked for a standard MSA and preliminary SOW for dedicated pilot — we'll push drafts after the exec sync.
[09:15] Markus Chen: ok thanks. last thing — can you add an example of the rollback trigger (e.g., 2% drop in pass-rate on clinic prompts) in the doc?
[09:24] Priya Nair: yes, we'll include objective triggers and sample rate thresholds.
[09:29] Liam Ortega: perfect. thanks all — we'll follow up in the next 48 hours with artifacts.
[09:35] Speaker 6: thanks
[09:37] Meeting end

Notes and references:
